title: Context Mosaic — quick readings + conference takeaways
content:
Quick brain dump from reading sprint + Bay Area workshop (notes to self). Intent: surface small experiments to run (1-2 wk) and anchor references. Not polished — fragments, TODOs, and rough hypotheses.

1) High-level themes noticed across papers + talks
- Attention as a substrate for fast-context stitching rather than just pairwise scores — good talks from ‘Attention Mosaic’ workshop: compositional attention blocks, tiled attention. Implication: maybe we can do a hybrid tile+kv approach for long sessions to reduce per-token compute.
- KV compression (quantized/learned): many groups use small bottleneck transforms to compress KV caches between segments. Tradeoffs: quality vs memory; seems promising for long context >50k tokens.
- Eval ergonomics: short probe suites reveal regression but miss subtle drift in retrieval+cache interactions. Need layered probes (prefix, retrieval-merged, conversational).

2) Papers / posts to prioritize (skim -> implement probes)
- "Mosaic Attention: Efficient Long-Range Composition" (workshop talk notes) — focus on tiled attention that composes local blocks with a sparse interconnect. Quick take: good for episodes with local coherence + occasional long-range refs. Action: get toy implementation or reuse tiled kernels in runtime.
- "Bottlenecked KV Compression for Episodic Memory" — uses small MLP bottleneck on KV states; reported minimal degradation on QA but big memory wins. Action: reproduce on small Llama-like model with 8k->64k sessions.
- "Prefix-preserving caching for generation quality" (blog) — nice heuristics for eviction and prefix-aware reuse. Action: codify eviction signal and add telemetry hooks in console.

3) Experimental ideas (priority and quick notes)
- A: KV micro-compression experiment (1 week)
  - Dataset: 500 long-session chat transcripts (internal anonymized demo logs).
  - Protocol: baseline full float32 KV -> 1) 8-bit linear quant 2) learned MLP bottleneck compress->decompress 3) product quantization (PQ). Measure: end-to-end perplexity, QA accuracy, latency for retrieval+apply.
  - Success criteria: <2% drop QA accuracy vs 3–4x memory reduction.

- B: Tiled attention shim (2-3 weeks)
  - Goal: route long sessions through tiled local blocks + sparse interconnect. Start with CPU/GPU PyTorch prototype. If promising, open issue to explore kernel implementation for runtime.
  - Risks: kernel work could be heavy; need to measure latency curve for small batch sizes.

- C: Layered probes for caching/regression detection (1 week)
  - Design 3 probe tiers: prefix continuity, retrieval merge, hallucination drift (task-specific). Hook to Optimize quality monitoring to fire alerts when mismatch grows beyond threshold.

4) Implementation TODOs / tickets to file
- Create GH issue prototype: redwood/serving-runtime: add KV compression interface (pluggable compress/decompress hooks) — link to GH-issue in linked_artifacts.
- Add console telemetry: per-request cache hit ratio + compressed KV sizes. New panel idea: memory footprint heatmap over session time.
- Draft quick eval notebook: experiments/A_kv_compression_notebook.ipynb (internal), include sample transcripts and measurement harness.

5) Quick heuristics and notes-to-self from talks
- Don’t aggressively compress the most recent 2–4 blocks — give them higher fidelity; compress older context more.
- Eviction should be signalized by token-level novelty (simple heuristic: new tokens’ trigram overlap with cached context).
- For tiled attention, route by segment boundary detection (dialog turns, paragraphs) — cheap but surprisingly effective.

6) Open questions / hypotheses to test
- Does PQ-style compression harm coherent entity tracking across segments more than short-term span QA?
- Is hybrid tiled + KV caching better than either alone for retrieval-augmented dialogs?
- Can we build a synthetic probe that stresses entity persistence across compressed KVs? (Design idea: synthetic convo that references invented names across 40k tokens.)

7) Useful links I clipped in talk
- workshop slides: tinyurl.com/attn-mosaic-2029
- blog: prefix-cache heuristics (medium link clipped)
- internal confluence: kv-compression-playbook (linked above)

8) Next steps this week
- Monday: spin up baseline KV snapshot and measure mem/latency (A experiment).
- Tue: file GH stub + issue for compression plugin; ping Avi for kernel feasibility.
- Wed: sketch layered-probe templates and share with Mira for eval inputs.
- End of week: decision point — if A meets criteria, expand to tiled prototype.

Scraps / half-formed ideas:
- Idea: use a learned controller to decide compress strength per-block (cheap model that outputs quantization bits per block). Might be overkill.
- Note: check with infra about GPU memory reservation for long-run 64k sessions (talk to SRE).
- Remind: add microbench harness to measure decompression cost per token — if decompress is heavy, benefit disappears.

Random notes / phrases I want to save:
- "prefix fidelity matters more than raw size for QA"
- "tiled local + sparse global = practical long context"

References to file later in confluence and GH. Will iterate.

-- Keira
